select_permissions.comment: Profile of users who share at least one organization with the caller.

insert_permissions.comment: Layer 2 — a connection spends money and reaches an external endpoint, so only an owner may create one. `api_key` is writable but not selectable: the value goes in and never comes back out.

select_permissions.comment: `api_key` is absent from this column list, so a connection's key is never readable over GraphQL by anyone — not even the owner who set it. Only the engine reads it, with the admin secret. Every member may read the rest, because an editor has to be able to pick a connection for an llm_call step.

update_permissions.comment: `org_id` is not in the column list, so a connection cannot be moved into another organization.

select_permissions.comment: A notify step inserts here; the notification_created Event Trigger delivers it. Members can watch delivery status live.

insert_permissions.comment: Layer 1 — only an owner can add members, and only to their own org.

select_permissions.comment: Members of an org can see their co-members (needed for the members screen).

update_permissions.comment: Only an owner can change roles, and only `role` is mutable — allowing org_id/user_id to change would let an owner move a member into another org.

delete_permissions.comment: Only an owner can remove members; a DB trigger stops the last owner going.

select_permissions.comment: The aggregation view. Scoped through the same org_members predicate as every table — via a manual relationship back to organizations, so a member of one org cannot read another org's usage numbers.

computed_fields.name: avg_run_duration_ms
computed_fields.comment: Average wall-clock duration of finished runs in this organization.

select_permissions.comment: Layer 1 — you can only see organizations you are a member of.

update_permissions.comment: Owners may rename their organization. quota_limit is intentionally NOT updatable: a tenant that can raise its own quota has no quota.

select_permissions.comment: The table the UI subscribes to. Read-only for every role: approving a gate is a mid-execution decision, so it goes through the approveStep Action, never through a row update. Without this restriction a viewer could simply mutate status/approved_by and resume a paused run.

insert_permissions.comment: The "watched table" for database_event triggers. Inserting a row here is an ordinary business write (owner/editor), and the Event Trigger below turns it into a workflow run with no button click.

select_permissions.comment: Rows written by db_write steps. Engine-write-only, member-readable.

Read-only for every member. There is deliberately no insert permission for any role: a run can only be created by start_workflow_run() via an Action, which is what makes quota enforcement and "viewers cannot trigger runs" impossible to bypass from the client.

insert_permissions.comment: Layer 1 (owner/editor in the workflow's org) AND Layer 2: db_write and notify steps require owner. Expressed as: the caller is an owner, OR the caller is an editor and the step type is not one of the restricted ones.

update_permissions.comment: Same Layer 2 predicate on both `filter` (which rows may be targeted) and `check` (what the row may become) — without the `check`, an editor could create an llm_call step and then patch its type to db_write.

delete_permissions.comment: Editors may delete ordinary steps; removing a db_write/notify step is an owner action, mirroring who was allowed to create it.

insert_permissions.comment: Layer 2 — webhook triggers are owner-only. `secret` is not writable, so it always comes from the column default (24 random bytes).

select_permissions.comment: `secret` is absent from this column list, so a webhook secret is never readable over GraphQL by anyone. Owners fetch the full endpoint through the getWebhookEndpoint Action.

update_permissions.comment: `type` is not in the column list: a trigger's kind is immutable, so a manual trigger can never be converted into a webhook to dodge Layer 2.

insert_permissions.comment: Layer 1 — owner/editor only. `created_by` is forced to the caller.

select_permissions.comment: Layer 1 — any member (including viewer) may read their org's workflows.

delete_permissions.comment: Deleting a workflow (and its run history) is an owner action.

functions.comment: Increments organizations.quota_used at most once per run, guarded by workflow_runs.quota_counted. Returns the updated organization, or no rows if the run had already been counted.

Atomic run creation: re-checks membership/role in the database, checks quota against used + in-flight runs under a row lock on the organization, and inserts the workflow_run together with all of its step_runs in one transaction. Returns the created run.

actions.name: approveStep
actions.comment: Clears a paused approval_gate. The handler re-checks the approver's org role (Layer 2, mid-execution) before recording approved_by/approved_at and resuming the run from the following step. This cannot be a row permission: it is a decision about a run in flight, not a row read or write.

actions.name: createOrganization
actions.comment: Creates an organization and the caller's owner membership in one nested insert, so an org can never exist without an owner. Needs the admin secret to write the membership row for a user who is not yet a member of anything.

actions.name: getWebhookEndpoint
actions.comment: Query action. Returns the callable webhook URL and secret for a trigger, to owners of that trigger's organization only. This is the sole path by which a secret leaves the database.

actions.name: rejectStep
actions.comment: The other half of the gate: records rejected_by/rejected_at and terminates the run as cancelled. Same role check as approveStep.

actions.name: rotateWebhookSecret
actions.comment: Replaces a webhook trigger's secret, owner-only. An Action for the same reason reading it is one: `secret` appears in no select or update permission, so no role can write it either. The new value is generated server-side and never accepted from the caller, and every previously issued secret stops working immediately.

actions.name: triggerWorkflowRun
actions.comment: Manual trigger. Verifies the caller is owner/editor in the workflow's org, checks the org quota, creates the run plus all step_runs atomically, then executes the steps in the background so the mutation returns immediately and the client can watch progress over the step_runs subscription.

actions.name: triggerWorkflowWebhook
actions.comment: Inbound webhook endpoint for external systems, exposed to the unauthorized `public` role: there is no user session, so authentication is the per-trigger secret (24 random bytes, never readable over GraphQL) compared in constant time by the handler.

actions.name: upsertOrgMember
actions.comment: Adds or re-roles a member by email address. An Action rather than a plain mutation because resolving an email to a user id requires reading auth.users beyond what any tenant is allowed to see.

objects.name: TriggerRunOutput
objects.description: Result of starting a workflow run.

objects.name: StepDecisionOutput
objects.description: Result of approving or rejecting a paused approval_gate step.

objects.name: WebhookSecretOutput
objects.description: A webhook trigger's newly generated secret.

cron_triggers.name: workflow_scheduler
cron_triggers.comment: Evaluates all enabled scheduled workflow triggers once a minute.
